title: The Larger Catechism and the Lord's Supper - Part 4: Preparation and Participation
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro
series: The Larger Catechism and the Lord's Supper
summary: This lesson examines questions 171-173 of the Larger Catechism concerning preparation for and participation in the Lord's Supper. Pastor Lyro explains how believers should prepare themselves through self-examination and renewed obedience, addresses who should partake (including those with weak faith and doubts about salvation), and discusses the church's authority to bar the ignorant and unrepentant from the table.

outline.title: How to Prepare for the Lord's Supper (Question 171)
subpoints: Self-examination is required before partaking, including examining one's faith in Christ, relationship to sin and sanctification, and pursuit of Christian obedience
Weekly preparation for the Lord's Supper serves as a means of grace, allowing believers to repent from sin and renew their commitment to obedience
Self-examination and renewed obedience are the two main components of proper preparation

outline.title: Who Should Partake: The Weak and Doubtful (Question 172)
subpoints: Those who lack assurance of salvation but possess genuine faith in Christ should partake of the Lord's Supper
Assurance is not of the essence of faith; a person can have true faith without subjective certainty of salvation
The Lord's Supper points weak and doubting believers to Christ and provides grace for their spiritual strengthening
The sacrament is appointed for the relief of weak and doubting Christians

outline.title: Who Should Be Kept from the Table: The Ignorant and Unrepentant (Question 173)
subpoints: Those who are ignorant of what the Lord's Supper means should be kept from the table until instructed
Those living in unrepentant sin should be barred from participation until they manifest reformation
The church has biblical authority to exclude unworthy participants through the power of the keys
Church membership serves as the means by which the church properly vets who understands and is prepared for the sacrament

outline.title: The Distinction Between Lack of Assurance and Lack of Faith
subpoints: Those with weak faith and doubts about salvation differ from those who falsely believe they are Christians
Objective marks of faith include believing in Jesus Christ, loving the brethren, and obeying God's commands
Foundation for salvation rests on God's knowledge of who truly belongs to Him, not merely subjective feeling

outline.title: Arguments Against Paedobaptism and Infant Communion
subpoints: The requirement for self-examination before partaking demonstrates the need for cognitive ability to understand the sacrament
Understanding of what the bread and cup represent is essential to proper participation
One must discern the body, understanding that they are part of the church, the spiritual body of Christ

outline.title: The Lord's Supper as a Means of Grace
subpoints: Preparation for the Lord's Supper serves as weekly meditation and devotion that shapes believers spiritually
The sacrament continues to dispense grace after the meal as believers reflect upon it
The elements point believers to Christ and His redemptive work on their behalf

transcript:
## Study of the Larger Catechism on the Lord's Supper

We continue our study of what the Larger Catechism has to say about the Lord's Supper. We should have just one more study on this next week, Lord willing, before we are done. Tonight we are going to look at questions 171-173 of the Larger Catechism. So far, the Larger Catechism has taught us what a sacrament is. It has taught us what the Lord's Supper is, specifically in question 168. And it has also taught us the mechanics of how to do the Lord's Supper. Tonight we will consider how we prepare ourselves for the Lord's Supper and who should partake of the Lord's Supper. Those are the two things that we're going to be looking at tonight.

## Question 171: How to Prepare for the Lord's Supper

As we talk about the first subject, how to prepare for the Lord's Supper, and as we read through question 171, think of how these activities that the question and answer will enumerate can be a great Sunday morning meditation as we prepare for the Lord's Supper every week. This can be something we do every single week. It doesn't have to be long. It can be something that is a blessing for us as we do that.

### The Text of Question 171

Question 171 asks: "How are they that receive the sacrament of the Lord's Supper to prepare themselves before they come unto it?"

Answer: "They that receive the sacrament of the Lord's Supper are, before they come, to prepare themselves thereunto by examining themselves of their being in Christ, of their sins and wants, of the truth and measure of their knowledge, faith, and repentance, love to God and the brethren, charity to all men, forgiving those that have done them wrong, of their desires after Christ and of their new obedience by renewing the exercise of these graces by serious meditation and fervent prayer."

The preparation for the Lord's Supper consists of two main things: self-examination and renewed obedience. All the phrases and clauses in this answer bow down to these two things. Most of them talk about self-examination and then the last little bit of it is about renewed obedience as we prepare to come to the Lord's Supper.

### Self-Examination Is Required

Just to state the obvious, self-examination is required in preparation for partaking of the Lord's Supper. We see that in 1 Corinthians 11:28:

> "But let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of the bread and drink of the cup."

Self-examination precedes coming to the supper. This is one of the reasons why we do not believe in paedobaptism—that babies should take of the elements. The Bible requires a certain cognitive level in order to examine oneself to see if they should come to the Lord's Supper.

The catechism says that we are to examine ourselves about the reality of our faith—whether we are in Christ. The Bible teaches that we are to make sure we examine ourselves as to whether we are in the faith. As Paul says in 2 Corinthians 13:5:

> "Test yourselves, do you not know yourselves that Jesus Christ is in you? Unless indeed you are disqualified. But I trust that you will know that we are not disqualified."

Test yourself, examine yourself to see if you are in the faith. The weekly Lord's Supper, as we prepare for it, gives us the opportunity to examine whether we are in Christ.

### Examining Our Relationship to Sin and Sanctification

Also, the question says we are to examine where we are in our relationship to sin and sanctification. Several of those clauses relate to that. In 1 Corinthians 10, Paul says:

> "You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons. You cannot partake the Lord's table and the table of demons. Do you provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than he?"

Where are we in relation to sin and sanctification? Are we trying to live a life that includes both fellowship with God and the world? Are we trying to entertain sin in our hearts and treasure it and keep it? Preparation for the Lord's Supper helps us to see those things and to repent.

Let's say you examine yourself and you realize that you are harboring sin in your heart that is dear to you. The logical thing to do is not to say that therefore you should not take the Lord's Supper. The right thing is to repent at that moment and be ready to take of the Lord's Supper. You should never make provision for the flesh. Never make provision to keep that sin that is so dear to you. As some have said, kill sin or it will kill you. If it's complicated, get rid of it. That's pretty much it.

### Examining Our Christian Life

Also, the catechism teaches that we are examining ourselves to see whether we are living a Christian life—the truth and measure of our obedience. Some of these clauses approach the same subject from different angles to help us think about it more fully. Each of these clauses is not necessarily talking about something completely different, but it's just a slight change in the wording so that we can think about the same thing from all kinds of different angles.

We are to examine our lives to see where we are according to truth and the measure of our obedience. Paul says in 1 Corinthians 11:31-32:

> "For if we would judge ourselves, we would not be judged. But when we are judged, we are chastened by the Lord that we may not be condemned with the world."

If we examine ourselves, judging ourselves, we don't need to be judged. In 1 Corinthians 10:23, Paul says:

> "Therefore flee from idolatry. I speak as to wise men; judge for yourselves what I say. The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not the communion of the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of Christ? For we, though many, are one bread and one body, for we all partake of that one bread."

Flee from idolatry as you come to the table. Where are you living? How are you living? Is your life lived as a Christian?

### Love, Unity, and Forgiveness

The catechism also encourages us to examine ourselves to see where we are in loving God and loving others, including forgiveness. Notice that forgiveness is mentioned. Why do you think that? Remember Matthew 5:23-24, which says when you are on your way to the temple to bring a gift to the Lord and you remember that somebody has an issue with you, drop the gift and go solve that and then go ahead and worship the Lord.

Forgiveness is important. Also, what we saw in the previous study in 1 Corinthians 10, we are part of the same loaf, the same bread. We are part of the same body. Unity is also important as we observe the Lord's Supper. It represents union. So that should be present with us as well.

### Renewing Our Obedience

The catechism also says that we are to renew our pursuit of obedience. As we examine ourselves as we prepare to come to the table, we are also renewing our obedience to the Lord. We have the opportunity to do that every single week if we take advantage of this opportunity to renew our obedience to the Lord. The book of Hebrews 10:19-21 says:

> "Therefore, having boldness to enter the holiest by the blood of Jesus, by a new and living way which he consecrated for us through the veil, that is, his flesh, and having a high priest over the house of God..."

These things being true, verses 22-23 tell us what we do:

> "Let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience and our bodies washed with pure water. Let us hold fast the confession of our hope without wavering, for he who promised is faithful."

As we think about the blood of Jesus Christ and his ministry as a high priest, which the Lord's Supper speaks about, then we are able to do these two "let us" statements, which represent a renewal of obedience. It is to walk further into obedience. As we prepare ourselves for the Lord's Supper, we have the opportunity to do these things. It's to be more committed to the Lord.

You can see that even before we partake of the Lord, as we think about it and prepare ourselves, it is already becoming a means of grace to make us more like Jesus Christ as we repent from sin and we have a renewed effort towards obedience.

## Question 172: May the Doubtful Come to the Lord's Supper?

Question 172 asks: "May one who doubteth of his being in Christ or of his due preparation come to the Lord's Supper?"

Answer: "One who doubteth of his being in Christ or of his due preparation to the sacrament of the Lord's Supper may have true interest in Christ, though he be not yet assured thereof, and in case he be duly affected with the apprehension of the want of it, and a sincere desire to be found in Christ and to depart from iniquity, in which case, because promises are made and the sacrament is appointed for the relief even of weak and doubting Christians, he is to be exhorted to his unbelief and labor to have his doubts resolved; and so doing, he may and ought to come to the Lord's Supper that he may be further strengthened."

### Understanding Assurance and Faith

What does the question mean when it says one who "doubteth of his being in Christ"? It is referring to assurance. One who doesn't have assurance of salvation is the one who doubteth to be in Christ.

What the question is saying, and what the answer affirms, is that the Lord's Supper is for the believer independently of the strength of his or her faith. In our understanding, assurance is not of the essence of faith. That is, one can have true faith in Christ and not be assured of it. Our confession makes that distinction, which is a big difference from the churches that follow the Three Forms of Unity: the Belgium Confession, the Heidelberg Catechism, and the Canons of Dort.

In the Heidelberg Catechism, question 86 essentially says that if you don't have assurance, you don't have faith. So in Dutch churches, you may have a congregation of 700 people where maybe 10 will take the Lord's Supper because they make that standard of assurance very high. That is not true of a Dutch denomination like the Heidelberg Catechism Reformed Congregations. But we believe that assurance is not required for you to take the Lord's Supper. Assurance is not of the essence of faith, which means that a person doesn't have to be certain that he or she is saved in order to actually be saved.

### The Evidence of True Faith

Can you think of a passage that might teach that? First John 5:13 says:

> "These things I have written to you who believe in the name of the Son of God, that you may know that you have eternal life."

He is writing to those who believe already so that they may know that they have eternal life. They may be questioned about it. They don't necessarily know they are certain, but they did believe.

How can somebody believe and not have assurance? Well, the experience of someone who is really not certain if he is saved is someone who is doubting, but he wants to and he loves Jesus and he wants to obey his word and all that, but he doesn't have that subjective inner peace that he is indeed in Christ. And yes, he wants to please Christ. Yes, he wants to follow Christ. That is the kind of person that this question is talking about.

A deep concern about one's personal salvation together with a desire to be found in Christ and to depart from iniquity is evidence of being saved, even though the person may not have subjective assurance.

Remember how John speaks in objective terms when it comes to faith. So you want to know if you're saved? Do you believe in the Jesus of the Bible? Do you love the brethren? Do you obey the commands of God? Those are three objective tests that he has given to the church.

Paul talks about faith. Assurance is not being of the essence of faith. He says in Philippians 3:

> "I count all things loss for the excellence of the knowledge of Christ..."

And he continues to pursue that knowledge of Christ. Paul won't pursue the believer. When Paul tells Timothy about the foundation of God, he does include assurance of salvation. He says in 2 Timothy 2:19:

> "Nevertheless the solid foundation of God stands, having this seal: 'The Lord knows those who are His,' and 'Let everyone who names the name of Christ depart from iniquity.'"

It doesn't say, "Let everyone who knows the name of Christ have this feeling in his heart." It says, "Those that name Christ just live a holy life."

### How the Lord's Supper Strengthens the Doubting

This question tells us that the Lord's Supper provides grace and points the weak to Christ, points those who lack assurance to Christ. How does the Lord's Supper point those who are struggling with these doubts—not because of sin, but because of a lack of inward assurance—to Christ? By reminding them of what Christ did for them.

Are you confident of this? Can you say it as a statement? Yes, the remembrance is one of the things that the sacrament does. Jesus says in 1 Corinthians 11:24-25:

> "For this is my body broken for you; do this in remembrance of me. This cup is the new covenant in my blood; do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of me."

As we do that, we are thinking about what Christ did for us. First Corinthians 11:26 says:

> "For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord's death till he comes."

As we partake of the Lord's Supper, we are being pointed to Christ. You remember Him. This is my body broken for you. This is my blood, which is shed for you. So as you are practicing the Lord's Supper and observing these things, they are pointing you to Christ.

The Westminster Shorter Catechism, together with the Westminster Larger Catechism, is a better theological catechism than the Heidelberg Catechism. The Heidelberg is a better devotional catechism. I encourage you to go back home and find the question on the Lord's Supper in the Heidelberg. It's beautifully written. It talks about how, as you hold the bread, you can be assured, as sure as you hold that bread in your hand, Christ is died for you. Very beautiful language like that. So read that as you think about the Lord's Supper.

So the weak and uncertain should come to the Lord's Supper, provided that he or she is pursuing Christ and obedience to his word. But if the lack of assurance comes from sin, then there is a different situation than what this question is describing. Because nobody should feel assured of their faith if they are living in constant sin.

## Question 173: Who Should Be Kept from the Table?

You can see that 172 talked about who should come to the Lord's Supper. Question 173 also addresses that, but from a different perspective. 172 is talking about the one who is a believer but doesn't have that inward assurance. 173 is talking about one who thinks is a Christian but was not.

Question 173 asks: "May any who profess the faith and desire to come to the Lord's Supper be kept from it?"

Answer: "Such as are found to be ignorant or scandalous, notwithstanding their profession of the faith and desire to come to the Lord's Supper, may and ought to be kept from that sacrament by the power which Christ has left in His church, until they receive instruction and manifest their reformation."

This question deals with those who think they are believers but are not truly converted. These are the opposite of the ones who don't have the subjective inner assurance of faith. These are the ones that think they are believers but they are not.

### Biblical Support for Excluding the Unworthy

Before we look at the scriptures, should people be kept from the Lord's table? Yes or no? Why? Scripture-wise, Paul says in 1 Corinthians 5. In 1 Corinthians 5, Paul addresses a situation of immorality in the church. Paul also speaks in 1 Corinthians 11:27-30:

> "Therefore whoever eats this bread or drinks this cup of the Lord in an unworthy manner will be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord. But let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of the bread and drink of the cup. For he who eats and drinks in an unworthy manner eats and drinks judgment to himself, not discerning the Lord's body. For this reason many are weak and sick among you, and many sleep."

What else? Matthew 18:15-20 teaches about church discipline and putting someone outside of the church so that you can see that the scriptures teach that people should be kept from the table. The question says the ignorant and living in unrepentance should keep people from the table. That is another reason why paedobaptism is not biblical. You need to understand. You need to not be ignorant of what is going on. Not a full understanding but at least know what does the bread represent. What does the cup represent? So they must not be coming in ignorance as well.

And that is why every Sunday we insist in the importance of membership. It is through the process of membership that one is properly vetted to see if they understand what is going on in the Lord's Supper for their own spiritual and physical good.

### The Seriousness of Unworthy Partaking

We read these things in the Bible and I think sometimes even we who believe the Bible would be true read them as something that happened in the past, that's happened in more if it's very distant. But the same God that killed directly people in Corinth for taking the Lord's Supper in an unworthy manner is the God who will kill people today for doing the same thing. Forget that that's the case. So membership is not a desire for an empire or control. It's actually a way to love the brethren, to love people, the neighbor, to make sure that they are not doing something that is harmful to them. Because it is not only physically harmful but it is spiritually harmful to the person.

Paul says in 1 Corinthians 11:27-30:

> "In where he says that you have to be able to examine yourself, you have to be able to discern the body. You have to figure out what the blood and the cup and the bread is and that you are part of the church. The body here is not the body of the physical body or just the spiritual body of the person of Christ. The body is the church and the person has to have an understanding that you are part of the body in order to partake the Lord's Supper. And ignorance of Christ and what the supper is is also something that should keep somebody away."

Then he says, "I am supposed to discern the body." Again, another argument against paedobaptism, the communion that is apart from a credible profession of faith.

### The Power of the Keys

Now do you believe the church has that authority? Do you believe that the church has authority to bar people from the Lord's table? Yes or no? Where in the Bible do you find that? You have that in the Thessalonian letters and in 1 Corinthians 5. But there is also a basic principle uttered by Jesus Christ himself. It is the power of the keys in Matthew 16. The keys of heaven are given to the church. And Jesus says:

> "Whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven. And whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven."

Most English translations give the idea that what the church does then will happen in heaven. But it's not the way it's written. It literally says what you bind on earth will have been bound in heaven. That they actually have preceded the church; the church only declares it. So the power of the keys given to the church, given to the elders, is a part of declaring what the Bible says concerning who should come to the table and not, and to keep people on that basis to open the table and to lock the table. That is another element of membership. That is one of the ways that we open the table is through the process of membership.

## Looking Ahead

The Lord willing, next Wednesday, we are going to finish the two questions left. We have seen how we should prepare ahead of time. Next week we are going to look at the Lord's Supper and what we should be doing as we are partaking of the Lord's Supper. Sometimes I do not know what to do. You put the bread in your mouth and then you wonder, what should I be doing? Or you forget to do something or you think, man, does this person sound loud? A lot of tree noises going on here. Your mind goes in all kinds of different directions and you forget what is it that I should be doing here that I am partaking of the Lord's Supper. Well, I will go ahead and see you next week. And then what we do afterwards as we go home—as we think about it, the Lord's Supper keeps dispensing grace as you think about it afterwards as well. So that is the goal for next Wednesday, Lord willing.
